worker: m test` passes: 9 tests, 0 failures, including `src/index.test.js`.

- **`src/kv.js`:** `createStore({ now = Date.now } = {})` returns a store with `set`, `get`, `has`, `delete`, `size()` and `entries()`, backed by a Map. Expired keys are removed lazily when accessed. `Date.now` appears only once, as the default for `now`.
- **`src/kv.test.js`:** it uses a fake clock and no timers. It covers all the cases you listed. It also checks that `entries()` returns a fresh array, so changing the array doesn't change the store.

No other files changed. Git printed a warning that LF line endings in the two new files will be converted to CRLF the next time it touches them. The commit still went through.

verifier:  four readers hide expired keys through the same `live()` helper: `get` at `src/kv.js:20`, `has` at `:24`, `size` at `:34` and `entries` at `:41`.

## Minor test weakness (not a failure)

The default-clock test at `src/kv.test.js:96-98` sets a key without a ttl, so `now()` is never actually called (`src/kv.js:16` only calls it for a numeric `ttlMs`, and `:7` short-circuits on `null`). The test therefore proves that `createStore()` works with no arguments and that `Date.now` appears once in the source, but it does not run the default clock. I confirmed the default by reading `src/kv.js:1`. A set with a `ttlMs` in that test would close the gap.

I changed no files and created no scratch files.
